title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: six-class (negation + GLV) parallel Pollard rho in G1, exact 18-instruction |y| key, five-instruction carry-exact V1 row, 142-instruction step ledger with three instructions of stated slack, R=2^16 twisted table, hard-bounded report store, global work meter at 2^126.302

claims.statement: For a uniform challenge T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1 (T=infinity returns 0), the algorithm of proof.md outputs x with success probability at least 0.39 (0.3901659), and on every run its total work is at most 2^126.302 batched-affine-G1-addition equivalents (C=2,000 instructions), enforced by a global work meter that charges every action an upper-bound price before execution and halts with failure at 2^126.302. The algorithm is parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho (2^20 walks, distinguished probability 2^-64, trail length cap 20*2^64, trail starts hard-capped at 2^63.25) on the (r-1)/6 = 2^252.2721269 classes of G1 under negation and phi(x,y)=(beta*x,y)=[lambda]. The class key is K=|y|=min(y,p-y), computed exactly by the six-limb rule of proof.md section 1 (p-y by six subs, a six-limb compare of y against ceil(p/2) by six sbcs, six csel: 18 instructions), with no top-bit test and no tie fallback. The canonical twist index is decided exactly from a 12-limb-product truncated fixed-point product, whose V1 term ((PH0*L>>64)+PH1*L)>>64 is computed in five instructions (umulh, mul, umulh, adds, adc) with both full 64x64 products and the carry out of adding the high half of PH0*L to the low half of PH1*L accounted for, and a metered exact fallback on near-ties (0.25 units). An R=2^16 twisted table makes every step one batched affine addition plus a 139-instruction ledger and 3 more instructions of stated rounding slack, so an ordinary step costs 1+142/2000=1.071 units, a cycle-traversal step 1.083 and a doubling 1.5 (7M+128=2,461.3 instructions, 2,464.3 with the same slack, below 3,000=1.5 units; M=C/6=333.33), where the doubling's 2y denominator joins the same Montgomery inversion batch as the additions, so no doubling is ever a small batch. 2-cycles and cycles of length <=64 are escaped by doubling the cycle's minimum 192-bit-fingerprint class (a class map; no cancellation can close a cycle through doublings since the order of 2 mod r is 2^250.8571), so trails meeting a common class reunite by the merging lemma. Fresh uniform trail coefficients are stored in full and collisions are solved by re-walking with coefficients reduced mod r and x=(e_2-e_1)/(f_1-f_2) mod r verified before output. The report store is hard-bounded, not bounded in expectation: 2^65 slots of 112 bytes (14 64-bit limbs) with double hashing, at most 96 probes per insertion at 0.15 units each, charged probe by probe, so at most D_cap*96*0.15=2^67.09 units over D_cap=2^63.25 insertions and at most 2^63.25*2^12=2^75.25 units for the starts, with store overflow bounded at 2^-40 under the stated random-oracle assumption H2. Phase 1 stops when a hard operation counter reaches S_ops=1.05*S0=2^126.1996225 with S0=sqrt(2N'*ln(1/0.6094)) and N'=((r-1)/6)*2^16/(2^16-1), so heuristic H1 gives P(T_c<=S_ops)>=0.3906; phase 2 completes open trails. The deterministic charge is 1.071*(S_ops+2^60)=2^126.2985810, hard extras are 2^95.471698 (phase 2 dominates), expected random surcharges are 2^106.409287 and the headroom at the cap is 2^117.579312, so the meter's early-halt probability is at most 0.000433998 by Markov and the remaining failure events total below 1.0e-7 (two-trail cap tail 2*21e^-20=8.66e-8 and three 2^-40 bounds). W = 2^126.3016727 <= W_up = 104855684481168075414614794644037112765, and 126.302 is the exact three-decimal ceiling of log2 W_up, checked with integers (2^126302 >= W_up^1000 > 2^126301). Peak memory is 2^71.8074 bytes with 128-bit addressing of the report table (below 2^72); preprocessing (report-table initialisation 2^57.84, jump table 2^28, first starts 2^32, sampling 2^21, expected below 2^57.85) is capped at 2^59 units inside W; there is no advice. This is a generic attack: no pairing, no number field sieve.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on BLS12-381 G1, check the GLV pair, orbit size 6 and the unit action, the |y| class key, uniqueness of the canonical member, the truncated-product twist index against the exact rule (random and adversarial near-tie inputs), the twisted-step identity, the doubling class map, the multiplicative order of 2 mod r, table entries, coefficient tracking on production steps, recovery of a planted x from two production trails forced to merge, and all three production rules at the six-limb production width along `prod_positions` (default 100000) real production trail positions: the 6-limb |y| key rule, the 6-limb twist index (with its fallback count), and the distinguished rule on limb 1 of K (bits 64..127), plus constructed keys covering every branch of that bit-range test with the partition index unchanged. Part B: run the per-trail algorithm of proof.md on a toy curve y^2=x^3+4 over F_q and report class visits to the first inter-trail collision against 1.05*sqrt(2N'*ln(1/0.6094)) and the fruitless-cycle rate; with pipeline=true the scaled production rules (phase-1 budget, sequential trails so phase 2 is vacuous, report capacity, 8-match cap) are applied and the success rate is reported. Then compare the same rule code at one 64-bit limb (the limb count the toy field needs) with the exact rules over `samples` sampled toy arrivals, and run a two-hash report store at load 1/2 with the 96-probe cap. The cost block prints the whole cost model of proof.md sections 3-5 from exact integers and 90-digit decimals, including the exact-integer check of the claimed score and asserts on the doubling cap, the small-batch count, memory and the success margin. Toy scale only.
